key_insight: Data-free PINNs show region-dependent accuracy in a deep lid-driven cavity, with floor-region velocity discrepancies below 5% but substantial remaining rotational-field discrepancies.
engineering_relevance: Regional validation is essential when assessing weak recirculation, because bulk velocity agreement alone can conceal locally important flow errors.
method: Hard-constrained streamfunction PINNs for steady 2D incompressible flow at depth-to-width ratio 5.
Prescribed regional collocation, transferred initialization, and selected residual-scaling and envelope variants.
Validation against independent spectral/hp reference solutions with the same Gaussian-regularized lid.
evidence_signal: At Re = 100–1000, evaluation on a 121×605 grid found 5.130–7.850% interior velocity discrepancies; a separate 161×801 assessment at Re = 1000 reduced this discrepancy from 5.624% to 2.658% with the refined workflow.
watch_item: Improvements compare accumulated finite-budget workflows, so they do not isolate regional sampling; configuration rankings also vary by region and observable.
paper_title: Regional accuracy of physics-informed neural networks (PINNs) for recirculation in a deep lid-driven cavity
